explanation: Maintain the smallest possible tail for every subsequence length. Binary-search the first tail not smaller than each value and replace it, or append when all tails are smaller.
timeComplexity: O(n log(n + 1)) time for n values. Each of n values binary-searches at most n tails, then performs one update.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. There is one tail per attainable subsequence length, at most n.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: For each length, tails stores the smallest possible ending value of an increasing subsequence of that length. Replacing the first tail at least as large as a new value cannot invalidate shorter subsequences and improves future extension opportunities. Appending occurs exactly when a longer subsequence is possible, so the final tails length is optimal.
walkthrough: For [4,1,5,2,6,3,7], tails changes through [4],[1],[1,5],[1,2],[1,2,6],[1,2,3],[1,2,3,7]. Its final length is 4, witnessed by subsequence 1,2,3,7.
edgeCases: The subsequence need not be contiguous.
Equal values cannot extend a strictly increasing subsequence.
The tails array represents optimal ending values and need not itself reproduce an earlier input prefix.
